newsitem.title: UK: UK Minister Simon to sell BP shares.
newsitem.headline: UK Minister Simon to sell BP shares.

text.p: Lord David Simon, Minister for Competitiveness in Europe, said on Wednesday he is to going to sell his two million pounds plus worth of shares in British Petroleum "as soon as the arrangements can be finalised".
The decision to dispose of the controversial shareholding follows publication today of BP's second quarter results.

Simon said he would give any profits from the increase in the value of the shares since he became a minister to charity. BP shares rose 40-1/2 pence on Wednesday to 862-1/2 pence after the company announced bumper second quarter profits.
The opposition Conservatives have hounded Simon over his shareholdings, saying he should have disposed of them before taking a post in which he was bound to take decisions which would impact on BP.
Simon chaired the oil giant until he accepted Prime Minister Tony Blair's invitation to join the government.
But Simon has insisted he has ensured issues directly affecting BP do not come across his ministry desk.
